deck.p3: Growtoo is a free grow journal: plant records, reminders, photos, weather planning, and an AI coach. The asset layer is optional — journal-to-proof infrastructure, not a token that leads.
deck.p6: AI that reads the journal, not a blog
deck.p7: Journal first, proof second. Growtoo turns a grower's ongoing plant history into structured evidence that can support more trustworthy, evidence-backed assets.
deck.h22: Hard to log. Harder to verify.
deck.p8: Grow tracking is often manual, inconsistent, and difficult for someone outside the grower’s process to verify. That makes adoption, collaboration, and any future investment model harder to trust.
deck.p9: Notes in chats, sheets, and memory
deck.p10: Gaps nobody outside the grow can reconstruct
deck.p11: A buyer or backer has to take the grower’s word
deck.h23: Log it. Organise it. Prove it only if you opt in.
deck.p12: Growers log plant activity, feeding, watering, growth stages, and photos. Growtoo organises that history into evidence. Selected records can then support optional Solana-based proof — verification-driven tokenisation, not a token for its own sake.
deck.p14: A structured plant history other people can read
deck.p15: Selected records can back a Solana seal
deck.p16: The product is already being tested on Solana Devnet with three early growers. They have been adding plants and logging activity about three days per week. This is roughly one week of early data — too little for retention claims.
deck.div19: ~3Days per week of logging
deck.div20: ~1 wkOf early data — present it as such
deck.p17: Useful as a signal that people will open the journal. Not a traction chart, not a cohort, not product-market fit.
deck.p18: A plant should become eligible for marketplace treatment only after it has enough documented history. Asset provenance has to be earned in the journal, not declared at mint.
deck.p19: Hypothesis, not a final rule. We are testing a coverage threshold — enough watering or feeding days across the trail, currently around half the days after a two-week window. The 50% lifecycle-logging bar is a hypothesis for testing. The exact rule can change with evidence.
deck.p20: The asset is supported by plant history, grower activity, photos, lifecycle coverage, and potentially grower experience signals. Tokenisation is how that evidence can be referenced — it is not the product by itself.

deck.p27: The round funds the work needed to test whether reliable grower data can become a trusted foundation for future RWA applications. The main risk is still unproven user retention and the legal structure.
deck.liYes3: Harvest-backed assets as a future application, not a live claim
deck.liNo3: Investment performance, or that current tokens have monetary value
deck.p28: If the journal does not retain growers, the RWA layer has nothing underneath it. That is the test this raise is for.
deck.p29: Product and engineering in one pair of hands — app, backend, programs, docs — built and deployed rather than outsourced.
